findings.issue: First-aid course teaches cooling a burn for ten minutes. In this UK-style health-centre context, current NHS guidance specifies20minutes under cool running water. Replace with that guidance or omit procedural duration. Source: https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/burns-and-scalds/ .

observations.issue: Clarify that the visitor receiving chest compressions was unresponsive/not breathing normally rather than merely someone who fell, so the narrative does not imply CPR for any fall. For example, describe a visitor who collapsed and was not breathing normally.
Explanation says jacket is where card was lost; script only says card was put in jacket pocket and is now missing. Prefer jacket was where she last put it.

coverage.scope: Full independent AI-assisted initial review of all 20 items:5 Listening,5 Reading,5 Writing and 5 Speaking. Read entire contexts, all 40 options,10 keys/explanations and every productive prompt/metadata field. Repeated contexts verified identical to shared contexts. No other reviewer reports inspected; no candidate edits or provider calls.
coverage.listening: Complete card-replacement dialogue read. Verified lost-card purpose, library use, $25 to $15 correction, payment before 2 p.m., next-day collection after 10 a.m., and passport/licence plus receipt. All five keys [0,2,1,3,0], all 20 options and all explanations checked.
coverage.reading: Complete first-aid timetable read, including leaders claim versus library example, all three November sessions, attendance/certificate conditions, registration deadline and capacity. All five keys [2,0,1,3,0] are textually supported. Burn-treatment duration is a blocking accuracy finding; CPR narrative clarity is separately noted.
coverage.writing: All five prompts read. Workshop category counts sum to 42,58,65 for March–May 2024; access-card replacement categories sum to 195 in each year. Both Task 1 datasets have complete units and dates. Three Task 2 prompts are clear, familiar opinion/comparison tasks. Word minima 150/250 and timings 20/40 minutes are explicit and consistent.
coverage.speaking: All five prompts read. Two familiar personal Part 1 sets; market-visit Part 2 contains four visible bullet cues, one-minute preparation and one-to-two-minute talk; two Part 3 sets require reasons and evaluation. Stage progression is appropriate for introductory practice.
